page: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 32 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. System memory is configured at 64.0 GB, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is supported by a 1890 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results show strong performance in memory bandwidth and specific computational tasks. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 211.12 GB/sec, and write bandwidth measured 102.72 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. The server demonstrated top-tier performance in Geekbench image processing and small-model LLM text generation. Multi-threaded Bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput also ranked in the top 25%. Conversely, the system is constrained under heavy memory-bound workloads, with large-model LLM text generation falling into the bottom 25% due to the 64.0 GB memory limitation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32lds_v6 offers a high density of compute resources and local storage relative to its memory footprint. By reducing the memory allocation to 2.0 GB per vCPU, the instance minimizes memory overhead costs for workloads that are primarily CPU-bound. This makes it suitable for compute-intensive applications, multi-threaded file decompression, image processing, and web serving. However, it is less suitable for large-scale in-memory databases or large language model inference tasks that require substantial RAM.
description: Microsoft Azure D32lds_v6 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine from the Dldsv6 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs, 64.0 GB of RAM, and a 1890 GB local disk. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance lacks a GPU but features advanced CPU instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmarks indicate strong performance in image processing, multi-threaded decompression, and small-model LLM text generation, alongside high large-block memory bandwidth. However, the low memory-to-core ratio limits its capability in large-scale memory-bound tasks, such as 70B LLM inference. This server is optimized for compute-heavy workloads, web serving, and local storage-dependent applications that do not require massive memory arrays.
